name: add_low_nibbles_as_digits
description: Adds the low nibbles of seven source bytes, walking from the last byte backwards, into a table entry chosen by a global index, carrying between bytes and storing each result as an ASCII digit. The routine is referenced by one unnamed caller and has no text references.

name: add_nibbles_to_table
description: Adds the low nibbles of seven source bytes into a table of ASCII digit characters, propagating carry from the least significant byte; the body matches the preceding entry. It is called by seven unnamed routines and has no text references.

name: prompt_restart_after_pause
description: Maps a status value from a called routine onto a result: one branch shows the text 'game paused (v1.0), restart game (y,n)?' and reads keys until Y or N is pressed, another toggles a global flag, and another returns one. It calls eight unnamed routines and is called by one.

name: process_active_entity_slots
description: Loops over a two-slot table of active entries, selecting each slot in turn and calling update routines; a slot whose check fails is cleared, and the outer loop repeats while two pending flags stay set. The facts list the text 'F.FIXIT' as referenced, but the code shows no direct use of it.

name: run_game_frame_loop
description: Starts by calling setup routines, then runs a long loop that updates several counters and calls a block of routines on each pass, returning early on several end conditions. The referenced texts '0000001' and 'demo.cmp' are listed, but the pseudo-code shows no direct use of them.

name: initialize_game_state
description: Sets a seven-entry global array to one, clears several counters and a flag, and sets another flag to one while setup routines run, then clears it again. It calls seven unnamed routines and returns the value from one of them.

name: initialize_global_state
description: Stores three constants into a global byte in turn, writes a constant word of 4095 into a table entry at an index derived from a global, and calls four unnamed routines to finish setup. It is called by three unnamed routines.

name: update_row_state_and_sum
description: Advances a stored row value by a fixed step, or resets it to a sentinel when it already holds the sentinel, then sums six bytes of the current row. When the sum is zero it clears a counter and sets the sentinel; otherwise it updates a state value from the flag word passed in and steps it to a filled slot.

name: update_row_state_from_frame
description: Performs the same row update as the preceding entry, reading its inputs from a frame relative to a base register: it advances a stored row value, sums six row bytes, and when the sum is nonzero it derives the state from bits of the flag word and steps to a filled slot. It is called by three unnamed routines and calls one other.

name: select_state_from_record_bits
description: When the state equals 16, picks a new state from bit flags in a stored record: bit value 4 gives 2, bit value 8 gives minus two, and neither gives zero, returning early when a further bit appears. It then steps to the next filled slot of a seven-slot ring, calls a routine, and stores a word from the record; it is called by one unnamed routine and calls three.

name: derive_state_from_flag_bits
description: Sets the state to two, minus two or zero from bit values 4 and 8 in a stored record, masks it into a small range, and steps to the next filled table slot before calling a routine. It then stores a word from the record and is called by one unnamed routine.

name: derive_state_from_flag_bit
description: Sets the state to minus two when bit value 8 is set in a stored record and to zero otherwise, masks it into a small range, and steps to the next filled table slot before calling a routine. It then stores a word from the record and is called by one unnamed routine.

name: reset_state_and_advance
description: Clears the state to zero, masks it, then steps backwards through a seven-slot ring until it reaches a filled table entry and calls a routine. It then stores a word from the record and is called by four unnamed routines.

name: advance_to_filled_slot
description: Steps the state down through a seven-slot ring, reversing direction at the ends, until it reaches a slot whose table entry is nonzero; it then calls a routine and stores a word from the record. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls three.

name: find_nearest_filled_slot
description: Searches a seven-slot ring outward from the current state in both directions for a nonzero table entry, storing the slots found and using minus one where a direction finds none. It is called by four unnamed routines and calls none.

name: increment_table_entry
description: Adds one to a table entry chosen by the argument's low word minus one, offset by a global row index, then sets a global to six and calls a routine. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: decrement_table_entry_step
description: Returns the current global state plus one, and unless that sum equals seven, decrements the table entry for the state, sets the state to six and calls a routine. It calls one unnamed routine and has no listed callers.

name: check_tile_collision
description: Converts a position into a tile index in a grid with rows of 41 entries, reads per-tile flags from a map table, and tests them against the blocking mask 126. It scans adjacent tiles along one axis and returns a count of tiles scanned before a blocking tile or a limit is reached; it is called by three unnamed routines.

name: forward_two_arguments
description: Passes its two word parameters unchanged to another routine and returns, with no other work. It is called by two unnamed routines and calls one other.

name: inspect_timed_out_routine
description: No pseudo-code was produced because the decompiler timed out, so the body is unknown. The routine spans 63 instructions and is called by two unnamed routines, but it lists no text references or calls, so its purpose cannot be determined from the facts.

name: recompute_table_entry_fields
description: Walks a table of seven-word records in global memory until a minus-one terminator, but only when a global flag is zero. For each record it resolves a pointer through a lookup routine, then recomputes the position and offset words from values read through that pointer, with an extra constant added to the first two records.

name: configure_blitter_copy_loop
description: Polls the blitter busy flag, then clears the blitter mask, modulo and control registers before looping over a parameter table. For each entry it waits for the blitter again and programs the source and destination pointers, the destination modulo and the blit size from values in the table entry and a global base.

name: load_graphics_branch_sequence
description: Makes the same calls before and after a branch on its flag parameter, and each branch issues a different fixed sequence of calls with constant arguments. The routine references the graphics files graphics/holder.cmp, graphics/iml.cmp and graphics/stills.cmp.

name: lookup_record_by_id_pair
description: Scans a table of twelve-word records for an entry whose first and second words match the two halves of its parameter. If the scan reaches a sentinel word above 999 first, it writes both values as three-digit decimal text into a buffer and returns the result of a lookup on that text.

name: refresh_record_table_entries
description: Walks a table of eight-word records until a sentinel word. When a global flag is zero it rewrites each record's position words through a lookup, updates per-slot state bytes in a loop, sets a status byte from a bit test and passes each record to a per-record routine; otherwise it skips the position and slot updates and only refreshes the status bytes and the per-record routines.

name: assign_record_flag_bytes
description: When a global flag is zero, walks eight-word records until a minus-one terminator. Each non-zero record takes the next byte from a global array into its byte at offset seven, and every record is then passed to a per-record routine.

name: update_tile_flags_loop
description: Calls a routine first, then takes a state from a byte in the record and, when the record's first word is non-zero, sets a flag byte and a second marker byte in a global structure. It writes the state into the top two bits of a run of table words, both at the record's offset and 41 words further on, with the run length taken from a byte field.

name: setup_blitter_copy
description: Waits for the blitter to go idle, then programs its mask, modulo, control and pointer registers so that source and destination share one pointer, and starts a blit whose size comes from the two parameter words. The pointer is the first parameter's word added to a global base.

name: initialize_state_and_process_table
description: Calls a routine on the global buffer with a fixed size argument, points a global at that buffer and zeroes five state variables. It makes two setup calls with constant arguments, then loops over a count held in a global, calling a routine with a word pair from a global table for each entry.

name: load_backdrop_and_format_digits
description: Calls several routines to load backdrop and graphics data, referencing the files backdrop/cmap0_am.cmp, backdrop/cmapd_am.cmp, backdrop/level_am.cmp and graphics/doll_hdr.cmp. It then writes five two-digit decimal values taken from a table into a text buffer, passing each to a routine, and loops over further entries when a flag and a comparison of two globals allow it.

name: iterate_five_slot_calls
description: Loops five times, computing a stepped argument from the loop index and calling a routine with it, with a call using that value and a global base before and after a conditional call. The conditional call uses a constant argument while the index is below a global count and a different argument otherwise.

name: copy_and_mask_tile_data
description: Copies 64 longwords from a source block reached through a structure pointer into a destination buffer, in four passes of sixteen with a stride of forty longwords. It then ORs a constant mask into every tenth longword over 64 entries and writes a fixed pair of bytes at two offsets relative to each of three ten-longword groups.

name: write_back_tile_block
description: Performs the reverse of the copy-out pass, copying 64 longwords from a source buffer back into the block reached through a structure pointer. It uses the same four passes of sixteen with a stride of forty longwords.

name: load_record_header_fields
description: Copies consecutive eight-byte blocks from a source buffer into the same global byte area, one after another, then reads word and longword fields from fixed offsets near the end of the buffer into individual global variables. The routine references the text strings 0000001, 0000100 and 9999999.

name: copy_tile_block_rows
description: Reads up to two control records from a byte stream, each giving an offset word, a width byte and a height byte, and stops early when the width byte is zero. For each record it copies a rectangle of words from the source buffer to a global destination at the same offset, advancing rows by a stride derived from the width.

name: format_count_and_refresh_entries
description: Writes the parameter value plus one as two decimal digits into a text buffer and passes that buffer to a routine. It then walks a counted array of fixed-size entries, resolving each through a lookup, calling two further routines when a field is not minus one, and copying two bytes from each entry into the resolved record.

name: update_entity_state_timers
description: Advances a timer word in a record and, after it passes a threshold, reloads two coordinate words and a phase from a table chosen by a lookup. When the phase is idle it tests the record's coordinates against two global positions and, if both fall in range, changes phase, updates a global counter or flag and starts countdowns; while the phase is active it then either calls a routine with the coordinate and a global value or steps the coordinate and decrements a countdown.

name: choose_candidate_from_flags
description: Builds a short list of candidate codes from two global flags and a byte field, adding a code of two for each flag that is zero and a code of one when the byte exceeds three. If the list is empty it returns a value looked up from a table, otherwise it returns a packed word with the candidate selected by the remainder of a routine's result and the quotient in the high half.

name: dispatch_state_machine_step
description: Dispatches on a global state value from zero to seven, calling a different sequence of routines for each case, and state two also sets a flag bit in the returned byte. It also steps a global offset with bounds checks and forces the state to six when a position global passes a threshold.

name: choose_move_direction_step
description: Reads a status word from a routine. When a status mask is set it updates a state word and returns minus one; otherwise it compares a first coordinate pair with a second to choose a direction code, a step value and a new state word, storing the results through pointer arguments and calling several routines for the lookups.

name: advance_movement_state_machine
description: Runs a countdown-gated state machine: when its timer expires it clears a block of state variables and reloads several fields from stored coordinates. Otherwise it compares absolute distances against thresholds, indexes an eight-entry lookup table, and calls an unnamed routine to advance the movement values.

name: step_position_with_timer
description: While a countdown is running this routine only decrements it, and on expiry it clears several state variables and calls an unnamed routine with a fixed argument. Otherwise it steps a two-axis position using an unnamed routine's result, clamps one coordinate to a range of minus four to 308, and reads an eight-entry table for the next value.

name: step_position_from_table
description: When its countdown ends it selects a twelve-byte table entry using an unnamed routine's result modulo a stored count, and loads two values from that entry. Each step it moves a position toward the entry's coordinates, clamps it to a range of minus four to 308, and once a hit counter passes 64 it calls a function pointer stored in the entry.

name: check_proximity_and_trigger
description: Compares absolute horizontal and vertical distances between stored coordinate pairs against small thresholds of four and two. When a pair is close and the related flag is clear, it sets a trigger and starts a countdown of sixteen, and when that countdown ends it calls an unnamed routine with a fixed code.

name: check_proximity_collision
description: When a state variable equals six, it builds a point from stored offsets and checks whether that point lies within a distance of four of two stored positions. A match sets the collision state to five and starts a countdown of ten, and the routine then calls an unnamed routine with the computed point.

name: initialize_global_state_block
description: Assigns non-zero starting values to the first three variables and zeroes fifteen more, with one of them set to all ones. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: load_level_graphics_table
description: Runs a long chain of calls to an unnamed resolver, feeding each result into the next call, and stores the resulting pointers in global variables. The referenced files are compressed graphics for characters and backgrounds, including audrey, bigcliff, cliff, candle and stars, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: set_entry_offsets_from_base
description: Stores the base horizontal value plus eight and the base vertical value plus sixteen into two fields, clears a third field, and sets two more to minus four and 240. It is reached only through a pointer stored in the data, not by direct calls.

name: store_four_in_record_fields
description: Writes the value four into two byte fields at offsets eleven and fifteen of a record reached through a global pointer. It is reached only through a pointer stored in the data, and this code does not show what those fields mean.

name: write_zero_one_record_fields
description: Writes zero into the byte at offset eleven and one into the byte at offset fifteen of a record reached through a global pointer, the same offsets the four-writing routine uses. It is reached only through a pointer stored in the data.

name: call_when_three_flags_met
description: Calls an unnamed routine with no arguments only when one flag is zero, a second is nonzero and a third is zero, and returns otherwise. It is reached from a data pointer and from three unnamed routines.

name: call_when_flag_pair_met
description: Calls an unnamed routine only when one variable is nonzero and another is zero, and returns otherwise. It is reached from a data pointer, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: call_when_flag_clear
description: Calls an unnamed routine with no arguments only when one variable is zero, and returns otherwise. It is reached from a data pointer, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls an unnamed routine unconditionally and then returns, so it acts as a plain forwarding wrapper. It is reached from a data pointer, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: call_when_three_flags_met
description: Calls an unnamed routine only when one flag is zero, a second is nonzero and a third is zero, and returns otherwise. It is reached from a data pointer and from three unnamed routines.

name: call_when_flag_pair_met
description: Calls an unnamed routine only when one variable is nonzero and another is zero, and returns otherwise. It is reached from a data pointer, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: call_when_flag_clear
description: Calls an unnamed routine with no arguments only when one variable is zero, and returns otherwise. It is reached from a data pointer, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls an unnamed routine unconditionally and then returns, so it acts as a plain forwarding wrapper. It is reached from a data pointer, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: clear_record_byte_eleven
description: Sets the byte at offset eleven of a record reached through a global pointer to zero and returns. It is reached only through a pointer stored in the data.

name: clear_record_byte_eleven
description: Sets the byte at offset eleven of a different record, reached through another global pointer, to zero and returns. It is reached only through a pointer stored in the data.

name: initialize_range_gated_fields
description: Checks whether a global value lies strictly inside a fixed numeric band, and only then sets one global to 5 or 0 depending on whether another global is zero. It also writes constant values of 4, 4, 16 and 0 into four further globals, and calls one unnamed routine according to the analysis facts.

name: initialize_global_constants
description: Assigns fixed constant values to five globals: 5, 4, 4, 16 and 0. It takes no inputs and contains no branches, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: toggle_flag_and_notify
description: Inverts the low bits of a global variable by XORing it with 3, then passes the variable's address to another unnamed routine. The callee is not named, so its role is only inferred from the address argument.

name: toggle_flag_and_notify
description: XORs a global variable with 3 and then passes its address to another unnamed routine. The code is identical to the other toggle routine in this segment.

name: toggle_flag_and_call_routines
description: XORs a global variable with 3, passes its address to one unnamed routine, then calls another unnamed routine twice with no arguments. The sequence is fixed and has no branches.

name: toggle_flag_and_call_routine
description: XORs a global variable with 3, passes its address to one unnamed routine, and then calls a second unnamed routine once. The control flow is straight-line with no branches.

name: toggle_struct_flag_byte
description: Inverts the low bit of a byte at offset 11 inside a structure reached through a global pointer, then sets the byte at offset 15 of that structure to 1. It has no branches and is reached through a handler table in the data segment.

name: toggle_struct_flag_byte
description: Inverts the low bit of a byte at offset 11 inside a structure reached through a global pointer, then sets the byte at offset 15 of that structure to 1. The code matches the other toggle routine of this kind in the segment.

name: toggle_struct_flag_byte
description: Inverts the low bit of a byte at offset 11 inside a structure reached through a global pointer, then sets the byte at offset 15 of that structure to 1. It has no branches and is reached through a handler table in the data segment.

name: toggle_flag_by_threshold
description: Compares a global value against 160 and, depending on the result, toggles the low bit of the offset-11 byte in one of two structures. It then sets the offset-15 byte of the chosen structure to 1.

name: toggle_struct_flag_b
description: Inverts the low bit of the byte at offset 11 in a structure reached through a global pointer, then sets the offset-15 byte of that structure to 1. It matches one branch of the threshold routine in this segment and is called by one unnamed routine.

name: toggle_struct_flag_byte
description: Inverts the low bit of a byte at offset 11 inside a structure reached through a global pointer, then sets the byte at offset 15 of that structure to 1. It has no branches and is reached through a handler table in the data segment.

name: set_flag_by_threshold
description: Compares a global value against 160 and sets the offset-11 byte of one of two structures to 1 depending on the result. The two branches differ only in the structure they write to.

name: set_struct_flag_byte
description: Writes 1 to the byte at offset 11 of a structure reached through a global pointer and returns. It has no branches and is called by one unnamed routine.

name: increment_struct_counter_flag
description: Adds one to the byte at offset 11 of a structure reached through a global pointer, resetting it to 0 when the result exceeds 4. It then sets the byte at offset 15 of the same structure to 1.

name: increment_gated_cycle_counter
description: When a counter global is below 4 or a second global is nonzero, it increments the counter and resets it to 0 once it exceeds 4. It then stores the counter in the offset-11 byte of a structure referenced by another global and sets the offset-15 byte to 1.

name: set_global_flag_to_one
description: Stores 1 into one global variable and returns. It is reached through a handler table in the data segment.

name: set_global_flag_to_one
description: Stores 1 into a single global variable and returns. The code is identical to the other single-flag setter in this segment.

name: set_global_flag_to_one
description: Stores 1 into a single global variable and returns. It has no branches and is reached through a handler table in the data segment.

name: set_field_when_conditions_met
description: Sets one global field to 12 only when two other globals are zero, a third global is nonzero, and the target field is zero. It is called by one data-segment handler and three unnamed routines.

name: set_status_when_clear
description: Checks three global values and, when the first is zero, the second is nonzero and the third is zero, sets the third to the constant twelve. The routine has no return value and no calls.

name: set_status_when_active
description: Checks two global values and, when the first is nonzero and the second is zero, sets the second to the constant twelve. The routine has no return value.

name: initialize_status_if_zero
description: Sets one global value to the constant twelve only when that value is currently zero. The routine has no return value.

name: dispatch_gated_position_band
description: Runs only when two globals are zero and a third is nonzero, then calls one of three unnamed routines chosen by a position value compared against two threshold constants. It is referenced from a data pointer table and from three other routines.

name: dispatch_clear_position_band
description: Runs when one global is zero and another is nonzero, then calls one of three unnamed routines selected by a position value compared against two threshold constants. It has a single caller.

name: dispatch_active_position_band
description: Runs when one global is nonzero, then calls one of three unnamed routines selected by a position value compared against two threshold constants. It has a single caller.

name: dispatch_position_three_way
description: Unconditionally calls one of three unnamed routines selected by a position value compared against two threshold constants. It has a single caller.

name: dispatch_position_two_way
description: Unconditionally calls one of two unnamed routines depending on whether a position value is below a single threshold constant. It has a single caller.

name: forward_to_subroutine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no conditions in the pseudo-code. It is referenced by two other routines.

name: check_and_set_flag_state
description: Checks two global variables and, when the first is nonzero and the second is zero, sets the second to a constant and writes one into two byte fields of a memory structure. It is entered through a handler pointer in data.

name: initialize_global_flag
description: Sets a global variable to the constant twelve if it is currently zero, and otherwise leaves it unchanged. It is entered through a handler pointer in data.

name: increment_cycle_counter
description: Increments a 16-bit global counter and wraps the result modulo five. It is entered through a handler pointer in data.

name: set_lane_flag_by_position
description: Compares a position value against a threshold and, on one side, sets a first flag to five when a related global holds the sentinel minus one and the flag is zero; on the other side it does the same for a second flag. It is entered through a handler pointer in data.

name: check_and_set_state_flag
description: Checks whether one global holds the sentinel minus one and another holds zero, and if both hold, sets the second to five. It has a single caller.

name: initialize_flag_by_position
description: Compares a position value against a threshold and sets one of two global flags to twelve when that flag is zero, choosing the flag by the comparison result. It is entered through a handler pointer in data.

name: initialize_second_status_value
description: Sets a second global status value to the constant twelve if it is currently zero. It has a single caller.

name: compute_tile_status_flags
description: Builds a status byte for a tile position by reading a tile table with rows of 41 entries and testing occupancy masks on the low nine bits, plus a two-bit pattern in the top bits, of neighbouring entries. The result is returned as a byte to a single caller.

name: scan_tile_region_backward
description: Scans a rectangular window of the tile table from a position toward lower columns and upper rows, returning the distance to the first entry whose low nine bits are set, or minus one if none is found. It is called by four other routines.

name: scan_tile_region_forward
description: Scans a rectangular window of the tile table from a position toward higher columns, returning the distance to the first entry whose low nine bits are set, or minus one if none is found. It has a single caller.

name: scan_tile_region_with_lookup
description: Scans a clipped tile-table window for the first occupied entry and returns its distance combined with a byte read from a secondary lookup table indexed by the scan offset. It has a single caller.

name: fetch_indexed_table_value
description: Computes a table index from the differences between two register pairs and a stack word scaled by eight, then reads a byte from a lookup table at that index. The byte is shifted, incremented and packed with high-order bits of a register to form the return value.

name: scan_grid_for_occupied_cell
description: Converts two coordinate words into grid cell indices by shifting right three bits, then scans a bounded region of a 16-bit map for the first cell whose low nine bits are nonzero. It returns a table-derived index for that cell, or minus one when no cell matches.

name: clear_seven_record_fields
description: Clears a global byte, then zeroes a 32-bit field at offset ten in seven consecutive 28-byte records of a global table. The record stride and count are fixed in the loop.

name: append_nush_table_record
description: Appends a 28-byte record to a global table while the fill counter is below its limit, storing a routine pointer, a longword and three words taken from the parameters. The referenced text 'NuSh' indicates the table entries belong to that game object.

name: set_proximity_threshold_flags
description: Once a stored counter passes a threshold, sets global flag bytes when a tracked word falls inside narrow windows around fixed constants. One pair of flags depends on the parameter equalling a specific value, and another pair depends on the parameter being nonnegative and below twelve.

name: clear_entity_table
description: Zeroes the first longword of forty 28-byte entries in a global table, then zeroes that field and a leading byte in the first ten entries. It resets the state of these entity slots.

name: invoke_record_handlers
description: Walks a counted array of 28-byte records and calls the routine pointer stored at offset ten of each record when that pointer is non-null. The record pointer is advanced by the record stride on each pass.

name: dispatch_entity_state_transition
description: Counts down a timer word in a record and, when it reaches zero, dispatches on a state byte stored in the record through a switch. Each case sets the next state, animation and position words and updates global counters; the listing is truncated partway through the switch.

name: stub_empty_return_routine
description: This routine is a single return with no body, so calling it does nothing. Several callers reference it by address, which makes it a no-op handler.

name: gate_entity_state_dispatch
description: Decrements a timer in a record and, once it has expired, checks a per-category counter capped at five before entering a state dispatch. The dispatch sets the next state, animation timer and position words, and the listing is cut off partway through the switch.

name: gate_secondary_state_dispatch
description: Returns early when a shared counter capped at five is full, otherwise increments it and runs the same state dispatch as the neighbouring routines. The dispatch sets next state, timer and position words in the record, and the listing is cut off partway through the switch.

name: gate_timed_state_dispatch
description: Waits for a timer in the record to run out, then for records whose second position word exceeds four hundred it limits entry through a shared counter capped at five. It then runs the same state dispatch as its neighbours, which sets next state, timer and position words.

name: load_position_from_pointer
description: Reads the pointer stored at offset twelve of the record and copies its first word into the record's first word. It also writes the pointed structure's second word, minus sixteen, into the record's second word.

name: step_position_until_target
description: Adds a signed per-frame step byte to the record's second word. When the sum reaches the target word it snaps to that target, clears the timer and runs the state dispatch.

name: store_word_at_offset_two
description: Writes the second data register's word into the second word of the structure pointed to by the address register. It is a single store with no branches.

name: step_record_byte_stream
description: Applies per-frame byte deltas to two position words while a counter is nonzero; when the counter is zero it reads the next byte from a stream pointer stored in the record. Depending on the byte's sign and value it stores step bytes, adds a signed offset to a word, clears two words, or falls through to the state dispatch.

name: accumulate_byte_and_advance
description: Adds the byte at the source pointer to a sixteen-bit word in the structure, then saves the source pointer advanced by one byte back into the structure.

name: gate_dispatch_on_source_byte
description: Returns early after clearing two words and an indirect target when the byte at the source pointer is nonzero. Otherwise it resets the record's timer and runs the state dispatch, which is cut off partway through its switch in the listing.

name: advance_position_by_tile_lookup
description: Converts the record's position words into a cell offset in a map with rows of 82 bytes, then reads three map words there. The top two bits of their combined value select a step from a table, which advances the position word; the state dispatch runs once the position leaves its allowed window.

name: reset_and_dispatch_state
description: Clears the record's timer word and then runs the state dispatch directly, with no timer or window check. The dispatch sets the next state, timer and position words and updates the global counters.

name: advance_record_state_machine
description: Increments a counter in the record and, when a masked test and a comparison against a global value both pass, appends a two-byte entry to a bounded buffer. It then switches on the record's state byte to set bounds and speed fields, update global totals and counters, and store the next handler pointer.

name: advance_record_state_variant
description: Performs the same record step as its neighbour, with the comparison value taken from a data register rather than computed from the record, and speed updates done in signed 16-bit arithmetic. It is called from one other routine and dispatches through the same state switch.

name: scan_grid_free_run_move
description: Reads adjacent grid entries from a row and column index derived from the position word and counts free cells ahead within a short fixed limit, adding that run length to the position. If the position passes a limit, it resets the speed field and runs the shared state switch, which stores a new handler pointer.

name: count_free_cells_forward
description: Steps forward through up to three cells using counters held in a second record and a base pointer, tallying how many are free before reaching an occupied one. It adds the tally to the position word and, if the position passes a limit, runs the shared state switch that stores a new handler pointer.

name: increment_or_step_toward_target
description: Increments the value at the record pointer while it is below its target field. Otherwise, if a global flag is set and a second value is within a bound, it moves the value three units toward the target, capped 32 above it or floored at it depending on a byte looked up through the record's index field.

name: conditional_step_toward_target
description: Applies the same flag-gated three-unit step toward the target as its neighbour, without the initial increment branch. It returns without change when the global flag is clear or the second value is above the bound.

name: clamp_value_to_minimum
description: Subtracts three from the first input value and stores the larger of that result and the second input at the address held in the pointer register. The only branch is the single clamp comparison.

name: dispatch_state_if_clear
description: Returns early when a global mode byte equals two or a status word has its low two bits set. Otherwise it sets a status global to three, clears the record's target field and runs the state switch shared with its neighbours, which stores a new handler pointer.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return and performs no work. One other routine references it, which suggests an empty handler slot.

name: dispatch_state_if_low
description: Returns early when a global mode value is greater than one. Otherwise it clears the record's target field and runs the state switch shared with its neighbours, storing a new handler pointer.

name: initialize_record_state_zero
description: Writes two 16-bit bounds into the record, sets the state byte to two, and stores this routine's pointer in the handler field. The bounds match the first case of the state switch in the neighbouring routines.

name: initialize_record_state_three
description: Writes a second pair of 16-bit bounds into the record, sets the state byte to three, and stores this routine's pointer in the handler field. The bounds match the second case of the state switch in the neighbouring routines.

name: classify_position_into_state
description: Checks whether a 16-bit position value falls within a band of six consecutive values, and if so sets the record's state byte to its offset in that band. Otherwise it picks one of two global pointers using flag tests and sets the state byte to four, then stores this routine's pointer in the handler field.

name: set_flag_and_store_handler
description: Sets a global flag to one, then stores a byte taken from the data register and a long taken from the address register into fields of the record. The caller supplies both values in registers, so this routine only writes them.

name: check_flags_and_set_state
description: Sets one of two global flags depending on whether the record's first word equals 82, then tests related globals for non-zero values. In every path it stores a global pointer in the record, sets the state byte to four, and writes this routine's pointer in the handler field.

name: set_flag_and_state_four
description: Sets a global flag to one and stores a global pointer into the record's pointer field whichever branch of a flag test is taken. It then sets the state byte to four and writes this routine's pointer in the handler field; two other routines reference it.

name: store_global_pointer_state
description: Stores the address of a global into the record's pointer field, sets the state byte to four, and writes this routine's pointer into the handler field. It has no conditional branches.

name: branch_state_on_word_value
description: Compares the record's first word against 80 and, on a match, sets a field from a global counter times 14 plus 1, copies a long global into another field, decrements a counter, sets a flag and writes state five. Otherwise it does the same with a second counter, a plus 8 offset, a flag and state six, then stores this routine's pointer in the handler field.

name: store_state_six_fields
description: Stores a 16-bit field computed from a global counter times 14 plus 8, copies a long global into another field, decrements a second counter and sets a flag. It finishes by writing state six and this routine's pointer in the handler field, and is called from one other routine.

name: increase_counter_by_hundred
description: Compares a position word against 301 and then increments one of two counters and adds 100 to its paired running total, choosing the pair by the comparison. It stores the new total in a record field, sets a flag byte, and writes state seven and this routine's pointer in the handler field.

name: advance_counters_rearm_handler
description: Increments one global counter and adds 100 to a second global, copies that value into an object position field, sets a flag field to 1 and a frame field to 7, then reinstalls itself as the object's routine pointer. Reached through a pointer in the data section from one unnamed routine.

name: step_split_counters_by_position
description: Compares an object coordinate field against 401, then increments one of two global counters and advances the matching global accumulator by 125. The accumulator value is written to a position field, a flag is set to 1, a frame field is set to 14, and the routine pointer is reinstalled; it calls three unnamed routines.

name: increment_counter_step_position
description: Increments a global counter and advances a global accumulator by 125, writes the accumulator into an object position field, sets a flag to 1 and a frame field to 14, then reinstalls the routine pointer. Entered from one unnamed routine.

name: decrement_split_counter_by_position
description: Compares an object coordinate field against 301 and decrements one of two global counters accordingly. It then stores a pointer to global data in the object, clears a flag field, sets a frame field to 8 and reinstalls the routine pointer.

name: decrement_counter_store_pointer
description: Decrements a global counter, stores a pointer to global data in the object, clears a flag field and sets a frame field to 8, then reinstalls the routine pointer. Entered from one unnamed routine.

name: select_layout_by_position
description: Chooses one of two sets of three object fields based on whether a coordinate field is below 301, and sets a frame value of 10 or 9 to match. It also sets another field from a global value minus 340 before reinstalling the routine pointer; it calls three unnamed routines.

name: initialise_fields_from_input
description: Writes constant values into three object position fields, sets another field to an input value minus 340, sets a frame field to 10 and reinstalls the routine pointer. Entered from one unnamed routine.

name: reset_position_and_frame
description: Zeroes one object position field, sets a second field to 100 and a frame field to 20, then reinstalls the routine pointer. It calls two unnamed routines and is reached through a pointer in the data section.

name: check_marker_and_update
description: Decrements a global counter, then compares an object field against 272; on a match it stores a pointer to global data, otherwise it sets another field to 384 and a state byte to 3. It sets a frame field to 11 and reinstalls the routine pointer.

name: set_state_and_frame
description: Sets an object field to 384, a state byte to 3, and a frame byte taken from an input register, then reinstalls the routine pointer. Entered from one unnamed routine.

name: set_flag_when_low_count
description: Sets a flag field to 1 when a global counter is below 6, stores a pointer to global data in the object, sets a frame field to 12 and reinstalls the routine pointer. It calls two unnamed routines.

name: decrement_and_add_offset
description: Decrements the object's first field, and when a global flag is nonzero and a global counter is below 6, adds that counter to a second object field. It then stores a pointer to global data, sets a frame field to 13 and reinstalls the routine pointer.

name: set_counter_and_frame
description: Sets a global counter to 1, stores a pointer to global data in the object, sets a frame field to 31 and reinstalls the routine pointer. It calls two unnamed routines.

name: snap_position_to_step
description: When a global flag is zero, rounds an object position field down to a multiple of 14 and adds 1. It then clears a flag field, stores a pointer to global data, sets a frame field to 6 and reinstalls the routine pointer; it calls two unnamed routines.

name: set_counter_by_position
description: Compares an object coordinate field against 401 and sets one of two global counters to 12 accordingly. It then sets an object field to 8 and a frame field to 33 and reinstalls the routine pointer; it calls one unnamed routine.

name: store_counter_and_frame
description: Stores an input register value into a global counter, sets an object field to 8 and a frame field to 33, then reinstalls the routine pointer. It calls two unnamed routines and is reached through a pointer in the data section.

name: decrement_counter_select_frame
description: Compares an object coordinate field against 401 and decrements one of two global counters; the matching branch sets a position field to 384 or 540 and a frame field to 17 or 15. It also sets a state byte to 3, clears a flag field and reinstalls the routine pointer.

name: decrement_counter_fixed_frame
description: Decrements a global counter, sets an object position field to 384, a state byte to 3 and a frame byte to 17, and clears a flag field. It then reinstalls the routine pointer; it calls one unnamed routine.

name: set_fixed_fields_frame
description: Sets two object position fields to constants 218 and 288, sets a frame field to 16 and reinstalls the routine pointer. It calls two unnamed routines.

name: check_marker_set_counter
description: Decrements a global counter, then compares an object field against 218; on a match it sets another global counter to 14 and a state byte to 21, and in both cases stores a pointer to global data. It then reinstalls the routine pointer and calls three unnamed routines.

name: init_object_handler_record
description: Stores the address of a fixed data item in a record's pointer field, writes a state byte copied from a register into another field, and installs this routine as the record's handler slot. The routine has one unnamed caller and calls two unnamed routines according to the facts.

name: init_record_with_counter_flag
description: Sets a flag byte in the record when a shared counter variable is below six, then stores a fixed data pointer, the state value 18 and this routine as the handler slot. It is referenced from a data pointer table and calls two unnamed routines according to the facts.

name: step_record_with_offset
description: Increments the leading word of the record and, when a flag variable is set and a second counter is below six, adds that counter to a word at offset 8. It then stores a fixed data pointer, the state value 19 and this routine as the handler slot.

name: arm_flag_and_init_record
description: Sets a shared flag variable to one, then stores a fixed data pointer, the state value 32 and this routine as the handler slot in the record. It is referenced from a data pointer table and calls two unnamed routines according to the facts.

name: snap_position_to_grid_init
description: When a flag variable is zero, rounds the signed word at offset 8 down to a multiple of 14 and adds 8, which snaps it to a 14-unit grid. It then clears a flag byte, stores a fixed data pointer, the state value 5 and this routine as the handler slot.

name: decrement_counter_set_state
description: Decrements a shared counter variable, then either stores a fixed data pointer or sets a second counter to 14 and the state value 21 when the leading word of the record is non-zero. The routine finishes by writing the state byte and this routine as the handler slot.

name: install_record_handler_slots
description: Stores a fixed data pointer in a record field, writes a state byte copied from a register into another field, and installs this routine as the handler slot. It has one unnamed caller and calls two unnamed routines according to the facts.

name: set_speed_by_threshold
description: Compares the leading word of the record with 161 and sets the word at offset 7 to 150 or 50 (depending on a flag) below that threshold, or to 100 above it. It sets a flag byte to one, writes state 22 or 23 respectively, and installs this routine as the handler slot.

name: set_timer_by_flag
description: Sets a word at offset 14 to 150 or 50 depending on a shared flag variable, sets a flag byte to one and the state value 22, then installs this routine as the handler slot. It is referenced from a data pointer table according to the facts.

name: set_fixed_timer_state
description: Sets a word at offset 14 to 150, sets a flag byte to one and the state value 22, then installs this routine as the handler slot. It has one unnamed caller and calls one unnamed routine according to the facts.

name: set_state_24_handler
description: Writes the state value 24 into the record and installs this routine as the handler slot. The routine is short, with no other fields touched, and is referenced from a data pointer table.

name: set_state_24_dispatch
description: Writes the state value 24 into the record and installs this routine as the handler slot, matching the state change in the neighbouring routine. It has one unnamed caller and calls two unnamed routines according to the facts.

name: assign_record_slot_position
description: Clears a flag byte and chooses a position pair and a data pointer from the leading word of the record, with the choice depending on a shared flag and a threshold of 161. It stores the record into one of two slot variables selected by parity of a shared counter, increments that counter, and writes the state value 25 with this routine as the handler slot.

name: store_record_slot_pointer
description: Saves the record address into a slot variable, writes two word values taken from registers into the record's first two words, stores a fixed data pointer, and sets the state value 25 with this routine as the handler slot. It is entered from several unnamed routines according to the facts.

name: place_record_in_slot
description: Picks a fixed vertical position from a shared flag, records the record address in one of two slot variables chosen by a shared counter, and increments that counter. It writes a fixed horizontal value and the position into the record, stores a data pointer, and sets the state value 25 with this routine as the handler slot.

name: store_record_slot_coords
description: Saves the record address into a slot variable, writes two word values taken from registers into the record's first two words, stores a fixed data pointer, and sets the state value 25 with this routine as the handler slot. It has one unnamed caller and calls one unnamed routine according to the facts.

name: register_slot_fixed_position
description: Increments a shared counter and stores the record address in one of two slot variables chosen by whether the counter is below two. It writes fixed word values 112 and 420 into the record, stores a data pointer, and sets the state value 25 with this routine as the handler slot.

name: store_record_slot_coords_copy
description: Saves the record address into a slot variable, writes two word values taken from registers into the record's first two words, stores a fixed data pointer, and sets the state value 25 with this routine as the handler slot. It is entered from one unnamed routine and calls one unnamed routine according to the facts.

name: swap_slot_record_data
description: Checks whether this record is one of the two slot records and, once both slot flags are set, clears the flags and counter, cross-links the two slot records, swaps their first 24 bytes, and sets state 26 with this routine as the handler slot. Otherwise it sets a second flag, clears the record's state byte and installs this routine as the handler slot.

name: set_flag_store_state
description: Sets a shared flag variable to one and writes a state byte copied from an undefined register, then installs this routine as the handler slot. The routine calls an empty stub and one unnamed routine, and the text fragment 'NuSh' is referenced from the surrounding data.

name: set_paired_object_flags_guarded
description: Sets a global flag to 1 only if a global byte is set, the offset-8 value modulo 14 is at least 7, and the difference between this object's offset-8 value and that of the object at offset 24 equals 7; a second flag is set to 1 unconditionally. When a global counter is below 4 it marks this object and the linked object at offset 23, then stores a pointer at offset 16, state code 27 at offset 22, and its own address at offset 10.

name: set_paired_object_flags
description: Sets a global flag to 1 only if the offset-8 value modulo 14 is at least 7 and its difference from the object at offset 24 equals 7, and sets a second flag to 1 unconditionally. When a global counter is below 4 it marks this object and the linked object at offset 23, then stores a pointer at offset 16, state code 27 at offset 22, and its own address at offset 10.

name: copy_object_state_block
description: When a global counter exceeds 3 and a flag is clear, it sets a global to 10, copies six 32-bit values from the object and six from the structure referenced at offset 24 into fixed RAM locations, and clears the offset-10 link fields of both structures. Otherwise it stores a pointer at offset 16, state code 28 at offset 22, and its own address at offset 10.

name: set_object_state_code_28
description: Stores a pointer to a global block at offset 16, the state code 28 at offset 22, and its own address at offset 10. It has no other effects.

name: reset_paired_object_state
description: Sets a global to 3, clears the byte at offset 23 on this object and on the object referenced at offset 24, then stores a pointer at offset 16, state code 29 at offset 22, and its own address at offset 10.

name: advance_linked_position_counter
description: Under a global counter limit of 13, it applies a test on the offset-8 values of this object and the object at offset 24 (a difference of 7 and a modulo-14 remainder above 6) and, when that test fails, increments a shared counter; once that counter passes 4 it copies a saved value into two counters. It then sets a flag to 1, stores state code 30 at offset 22, and writes its own address at offset 10.

name: initialize_object_pointers
description: Clears a global flag, then points offset 16 at one of two global blocks depending on whether a global counter is below 13. It stores a byte from data register D1 at offset 22 and writes its own address at offset 10 as the next handler.

name: increment_first_counter_and_rearm
description: Increments a global counter, then stores a byte from data register D1 at offset 22 and writes its own address at offset 10 as the next handler. The referenced text reads NuSh.

name: increment_second_counter_and_rearm
description: Increments a second global counter, then stores a byte from data register D1 at offset 22 and writes its own address at offset 10 as the next handler. The referenced text reads NuSh.

name: dispatch_object_state_machine
description: When the flag byte in data register D1 is nonzero, it clears the words at offsets 10 and 12, clears the link at offset 24 if present, and returns. Otherwise it resets the word at offset 14 and dispatches on the state byte at offset 11 across many cases, setting position and size words, adjusting global counters and flags, and choosing the next pointer and state.

name: dispatch_object_state_switch
description: Resets the word at offset 14, then dispatches on the state byte at offset 11 across many cases, setting position and size words, adjusting global counters and flags, and choosing the next pointer and state. It is the same switch as the flag-gated state machine but without the early clearing path.

name: update_grid_cell_bytes
description: Walks a table of 16-byte records ended by a sentinel value, and for each record steps a byte in a computed cell up or down depending on a flag at offset 7. It then writes the low two bits of that byte and a marker value into a run of cells, moving by a stride of 24 times a signed byte from the record.

name: invoke_update_routine_batch
description: Calls one unnamed routine 22 times in a row, then sets two global flags to 1 and 0. The pseudo-code gives the repeated calls no arguments, so the effect of each call is not visible here.

name: alternate_update_phase_batches
description: Alternates between two phases on each call by flipping a global phase value. Phase 0 makes 13 calls to an unnamed routine and phase 1 makes 9, each phase making one further call when a global flag is nonzero; the routine then flips the phase value and makes one final call.

name: clear_entity_state_flags
description: Calls an unnamed routine with a pointer to a global, clears three global counters, and sets the byte at offset 11 to zero for each of the twelve objects in a pointer table. If a global value is nonzero it calls another routine twice and sets offset-11 bytes on two objects to 1 when bit 64 or bit 256 is set in the results.

name: remap_table_entries_high_word
description: When a global flag is zero, it walks a list of 32-bit entries terminated by -1 and replaces each entry with the value returned by an unnamed routine called with the entry's high halfword. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: propagate_state_byte_chain
description: Runs two passes over a table of record pointers. Each pass computes a new value for a byte at offset 11 from the previous group's value, stepping it up or down through ten states with wraparound depending on a record's offset-11 byte, then writes that value and a flag at offset 15 into four following records.

name: store_call_result_constant
description: Calls an unnamed routine with the constant 624 and stores its return value in a global variable.

name: update_state_byte_from_table
description: Advances a 4-bit global counter by one, then sets the byte at offset 11 of the object held in a global pointer from a table indexed by half that counter. It then sets the flag at offset 15 of that object to 1.

name: initialize_paired_object_states
description: Calls the same setup routine as the flag-clearing routine, zeroes two counters and sets a third to 250, then reads two routine results: one sets a flag from bit 64, and the other sets the byte at offset 11 of two objects to 0 or 2. A third result divided by 137 gives a value from 1 to 4 written to the second object; when a global counter is zero, the flag is forced to 1 and both objects are set to state 2.
